subject: Customer-scoped log prune policy and verification steps
messages:
From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@solveta.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: security@solveta.com
Date: 2026-09-08T10:12:00Z
Subject: Request: customer-scoped log prune policy and verification approach

Hi Logan,

We are finalizing our SIG and CAIQ evidence pack for an upcoming audit and need a clear description of Redwood's plan for customer-scoped log pruning and how you provide verifiable proof of erase for tenants that request accelerated deletion (customer-specific exceptions).

Key asks:
- A plain-language summary of the prune policy (what categories of logs are candidate for pruning, retention windows, and exceptions for forensics).
- The verification artifacts you can produce (export IDs, sampling manifests, or proof-of-delete checksums).
- Typical timelines and handoff when a legal hold or SAR comes in.

We attached a template retention matrix and would appreciate a response by EOD next Tuesday if possible.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Reddy
Senior Security Engineer, Solveta Health
security@solveta.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@solveta.com>
Cc: security@solveta.com
Date: 2026-09-09T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: customer-scoped log prune policy and verification approach

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. I can provide an operational summary and an evidence bundle. Top-level answers below, and I will follow with artifacts and a short playbook PDF next week.

- Prune policy summary:
  * Session/debug traces and ephemeral inference keys: default retention 30 days; eligible for customer-scoped pruning to 7 days upon request, subject to active legal holds.
  * Application audit logs (auth, billing events): default retention 180 days; not prunable for customers except under a formally approved carveout with compensating controls.
  * Aggregated telemetry and metrics: retained 365 days and summarized; pruning is not applicable.

- Verification artifacts we can provide:
  * S3 export manifests with export IDs (sample attached file format).
  * Signed manifest that lists object keys and a SHA256 checksum for the exported bundle.
  * Optional: time-limited snapshot access for customer auditors (read-only URLs) for a sampling window.

- Timelines & handoff:
  * Standard prune request (no legal hold): 5–7 business days to complete and deliver artifacts.
  * Prune with investigation or SAR: paused; forensic team will assess and provide ETA (typically 10–20 business days depending on scope).

I'll send the supporting artifacts (retention-matrix.csv, a short prune-playbook PDF, and sample-export-ids.txt) by Monday. Let me know if you want these signed by our Compliance lead.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
logs-team@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:18:00Z
Subject: Internal: Solveta prune request — ask for artifacts + signing

Karthik / Neha,

Solveta (Priya) asked for the prune policy summary and verification artifacts; I drafted the reply (sent). Please help with the following so we can bundle and sign off:
- Karthik: can you generate a sample signed manifest that follows the current export pipeline (include object keys and SHA256 checksums)? We should redact exact object prefixes but keep enough detail for audit.
- Neha: confirm the SLA wording for 5–7 business days and the 10–20 business days for legal-hold cases. Also confirm whether Compliance wants the artifacts signed by the Compliance Manager or if a logs-team signature is sufficient.

I'll attach the draft playbook and retention matrix to the customer once we have the manifest.

Thanks —
Logan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: Solveta prune request — ask for artifacts + signing

Logan, Neha,

I generated a redacted sample manifest and added a signed wrapper (SHA256 over the manifest) per our export process. The manifest lists: 3 export IDs, object key patterns (redacted), timestamp window, and checksums. I saved as "sample-export-ids.txt" and included a short README describing redaction rules.

Notes:
- We should provide a reconciliation note: full export logs exist internally and can be reviewed under NDA; for customer-facing proves we use the redacted manifest + signed wrapper.
- SLA language: I'll confirm text with Legal for the exact 5–7 day phrasing (use "typically 5–7 business days" for now).

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime Ops

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@solveta.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: security@solveta.com
Date: 2026-09-14T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: customer-scoped log prune policy and verification approach

Logan — this is helpful, thank you. A couple of quick clarifications before we close the SIG entry:
1) For the sample signed manifest: will Redwood provide the signature as an RFC 5656-style detached signature or a signed JSON Web Signature (JWS)? We prefer JWS for automation.
2) For the time-limited sampling URLs: can you confirm the expiration window and whether the URLs are single-use?

If you can provide the signed manifest in JWS format and a sample URL with a 7-day expiry, we can close this item. If Compliance signs the manifest, please indicate the signatory name and title.

We appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Priya

---
Attachment stubs:
- retention-matrix.csv (CSV template returned with populated default values)
- prune-playbook-v1.pdf (short playbook with steps we will run for a prune)
- sample-export-ids.txt (redacted manifest with checksums and export ids)
